Penix is a low-end QB2 heading into Week 10’s home matchup against the Chiefs.

item.title: Samaje Perine rushed 11 times for 43 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons.
item.description:
Samaje Perine CIN Running Back

Perine had 43 yards on 11 carries, which was notable because he had two more rushing attempts than starter Chase Brown. While Brown continues to underwhelm, Perine is cutting into Brown’s ceiling (or lack thereof) more than he’s carving out a legitimate role for himself. Perine is one of the better handcuffs to stash, but he shouldn’t be in starting lineups in Week 10 against the Steelers.

item.title: Chase Brown rushed nine times for 57 yards in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three receptions for 18 yards.
item.description:
Chase Brown CIN Running Back

While Brown struggled in Week 8, the silver lining was that he out-touched Samaje Perine 20-to-5. After fumbling against the Titans last week, Perine actually had more carries than Brown (11-to-9) in Madrid. Brown saw all three targets that went to running backs against the Falcons, but there’s no way to spin this positively for the 26-year-old who had a preseason ADP in the teens. Brown still hasn’t scored since Week 1 and he’ll be an RB2 at best against the Steelers in Week 10.

item.title: Chiefs declared CB Mansoor Delane, QB Garrett Nussmeier, FB Ben VanSumeren, DE Jack Pyburn, OT Diego Pounds, and DT Peter Woods inactive for Week 9 against the Jets.
item.description:
Mansoor Delane KC Cornerback

The Kansas City defense will be without Delane against a Geno Smith-led Jets passing attack that showed out last week against the Raiders. The Chiefs this season are allowing the NFL’s 13th lowest EPA per drop back and rank 15th in drop back success rate allowed.

Source: Matt McMullen

item.title: Trent McDuffie (back) is inactive for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

McDuffie was a DNP in practice all week but still managed to get a questionable designation entering the weekend. That said, the team’s decision doesn’t come as much of a surprise given the fact that he was unable to get on the field last week. Fortunately for the Rams, they faced a depleted Commanders receiving corps, and they will have both Myles Garrett and Aaron Donald on the field for the first time together.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Browns declared QB Deshaun Watson, QB Taylen Green, C Parker Brailsford, DT Maliek Collins, LB Justin Jefferson, and CB Noah Igninoghene inactive for Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Watson cleared the league’s concussion protocol over the weekend but was not prepared as the starter throughout the week. Shedeur Sanders will get his first start of the season and Dillon Gabriel will back him up.

item.title: Colts declared TE Pharaoh Brown, LB Akeem Davis-Gaither, S AJ Haulcy, OT Charlie Heck, QB Riley Leonard, TE Will Mallory, and CB Justin Walley in active for Week 9 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Justin Walley IND Cornerback

No real surprises here as the Colts limp into their final game before the league’s trade deadline. That said there remains legitimate uncertainty surrounding the usages of Jonathan Taylor and Josh Downs, amongst others, in what could be their final game with the franchise.

item.title: Broncos declared S Talanoa Hufanga, CB Kris Abrams-Draine, S Brandon Jones, WR Lil’Jordan Humphrey, OG Kage Casey, TE Dallen Bentley, and QB Sam Ehlinger inactive for Week 9 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Sam Ehlinger DEN Quarterback

Hufanga was questionable entering the weekend due to an ankle injury, but will officially be sidelined for this one. The 28-year-old safety hasn’t played since Week 5 but was limited in back-to-back practices to close out the week, so there’s a chance he could return after the Broncos’ Week 10 bye.

Source: Chris Tomasson

item.title: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

With Skattebo down, the G-Men have been forced into a Devin Singletary start. Someone named “Gregory Desrosiers” appears to be the RB2. Expect a pass-focused game plan vs. Philly’s crumbling defense. Also inactive for the Giants are CB Colton Hood, CB Nikko Reed, OL Josh Sills, OL Marcus Mbow, TE Thomas Fidone II and DL C.J. Okoye.

item.title: Panthers declared LB Jaelan Phillips, QB Haynes King, CB Will Lee III, RB AJ Dillon, LB Bobby Okereke, OG Damien Lewis, and DT TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 9 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Jaelan Phillips CAR Outside Linebacker

Phillips and Lewis were both ruled out before the weekend, so there’s nothing too surprising to see here. The Panthers hope to end a two-game losing streak this week at home against a stout Broncos defense.

Source: Carolina Panthers

item.title: Dolphins declared RB Jaylen Wright, WR Jalen Tolbert, TE Justin Joly, G Christian Haynes, OT Chukwuebuka Godrick, CB Marcellas Dial Jr., and CB Reese Taylor inactive for Week 9 against the Lions.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

Both Wright and Kaytron Allen were questionable because of quad injuries. Allen is active and will serve as Ollie Gordon’s backup.

item.title: Commanders declared WR Treylon Burks, QB Athan Kaliakmanis, CB Fabian Moreau, CB Isaac Yiadom, and OG Tanoa Togiai inactive for Week 9 against the Rams.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

The Commanders find themselves incredibly thin at receiver with Burks (foot), Terry McLaurin (knee), and Dyami Brown (calf) all sidelined for this one. Stefon Diggs, along with rookie Antonio Williams could both be in line for busy days against a Rams secondary that will be without CB Trent McDuffie.

Source: Washington Commanders

item.title: Jets declared Garrett Wilson, Tim Patrick, Nahshon Wright, Joseph Ossai, Trevin Wallace, Kohl Levao, and Blake Freeland inactive for Week 9 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Garrett Wilson NYJ Wide Receiver

Wilson suffered a head injury last week and did not practice this week as he remained in the NFL’s concussion protocol. Look for Omar Cooper, Jr. and Adonai Mitchell to see more routes and targets against a tough KC secondary. Mitchell is likely to function as the team’s top wideout with Wilson sidelined.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

No surprises here as this was reported earlier today. St. Brown remains a top-flight WR1 for his matchup with the Phins. Sione Vaki is also active and will serve as the team’s RB2. Inactive for the Lions are CB D.J. Reed, EDGE DJ Wonnum, C Cade Mays, RB Jacob Saylors, TE Jordan Meeks, DL Mekhi Wingo, and EDGE Ahmed Hassanein.

item.title: George Pickens (hamstring) is inactive for Week 9 against the Colts.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens played through the issue last week but will ultimately be held out in Week 9. Tight end Jake Ferguson is active after failing to practice until a limited showing Friday. Ryan Flournoy steps into a featured role for the Cowboys against the inside-funnel Colts defense. Fantasy managers can insert Flournoy into rosters as a viable FLEX considering he leads the team in slot rate through the first half of the season. Also inactive for the Cowboys are LB DeMarvion Overshown, WR KaVontae Turpin, CB Joey Porter Jr., LB Tyrus Wheat, OL Ajani Cornelius, and TE Luke Schoonmaker.

item.title: Vikings signed WR Odell Beckham from their practice squad to the active roster.
item.description:
Odell Beckham MIN Wide Receiver

Beckham landed on the Vikings’ practice squad after being released by the Giants. He appeared in three games for New York and did not record any stats. Beckham hasn’t appeared in any games for Minnesota this year, but he’ll now be a member of their 53-man roster going forward.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that it “sounds like” the Jaguars are going to listen to trade offers for Brian Thomas Jr.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

The Jags have shot down all offers so far, but it’s hard to justify his current usage when the team could instead recoup some draft capital by moving him. Thomas hasn’t caught more than two passes in a game since Week 2. He has three games with zero catches this year and played just 19 snaps on Thursday versus the Ravens. The Chiefs are reportedly interested, though that would require the Jags to send BTJ to one of their biggest competitors in the AFC. The Steelers and 49ers are also reportedly interested.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is “pushing to play” in Week 9 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Skattebo was listed as doubtful for Week 9 after getting in a single limited practice this week. Players rarely suit up after getting the doubtful tag, but it’s not out of the question. Even if he is ruled out with inactives, the fact that Skattebo is pushing to play means he should be good to go for Week 10. Devin Singletary will handle the bulk of the backfield touches if he can’t go this week.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports the Broncos are hopeful Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) will play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Talanoa Hufanga DEN Safety

Per Fowler, he remains a game-time decision. Hufanga logged two limited practices this week before receiving a questionable designation. Before going down with the injury, Hufanga had one forced fumble and two interceptions, one of which he took to the end zone. Getting him back would be a big win for the Denver defense.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Hunter Henry (foot) has a “realistic chance to play” in Week 9 against the Packers.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

Henry only practiced once this week but still received a questionable designation on Friday. Eli Raridon would have taken his spot in the lineup, but it sounds like Henry will give it a go. He will be a high-end TE2 for his matchup with the Packers.

item.title: 49ers placed Christian Kirk (knee) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

Kirk missed the start of the year with a calf issue and immediately injured his knee in Week 7. The 49ers have already burned several injured reserve return designations this year, including one on Kirk himself. He could ultimately be stuck on IR for the remainder of the year, even if he’s not dealing with a catastrophic knee injury.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jaylen Wright (quad) will not play in Week 9 against the Lions.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

Wright had been backing up Ollie Gordon before going down with the quad injury. Kaytron Allen is the next man up for RB2 duties, though he’s also dealing with a quad issue. Needless to say, we’re expecting a large workload for Gordon this week.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Tanner McKee (rib) will serve as the Eagles’ backup quarterback in Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
Tanner McKee PHI Quarterback

McKee was demoted to QB2 after Week 8. He suffered a rib injury in that game, but is healthy enough to hold a clipboard. Joe Milton will make his first career start versus the Giants today.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Sam Darnold (quad) could “potentially” miss Week 10 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Sam Darnold SEA Quarterback

Garafolo added that Darnold is dealing with a cracked rib, though it sounds like the quad issue is what’s preventing him from playing. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald called Darnold “week to week” on Wednesday. They get their bye in Week 11, so holding him out for one more game to get an extended break makes the most sense. Fantasy managers should plan on Darnold missing Week 10 in addition to today’s game against Arizona. Drew Lock will start today. As long as his elbow issue doesn’t flare up, he will be in line to start next week as well.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport believes the Vikings are “a team to watch” for Daniel Jones.
item.description:
Daniel Jones IND Quarterback

Per Rapoport, the Ravens called Indy about Jones after Lamar Jackson went down with a potentially season-ending thumb injury. They eventually traded for Jacoby Brissett. With Kyler Murray hurt and playing poorly even when healthy, the Vikings are at least going to explore some outside options at quarterback. Jones was on the team’s practice squad in 2024 before joining the Colts last year.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports teams have “checked in on” Jadeveon Clowney.
item.description:
Jadeveon Clowney HOU Defensive End

Garafolo noted that the Texans’ game against the Chargers today will go a long way in determining whether the team wants to buy or sell at the trade deadline. Even at 2-5, the team thinks they can make a run at the playoffs. Clowney has been a hired-gun pass-rusher for most of his career. He isn’t starting for Houston and has just 1.5 sacks while playing a career-low 37 percent of the snaps on defense. If the Texans feel that their season is over, he will be one of the easiest players to move on from.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) will have a “full workload” in Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

McCaffrey went down with the hamstring injury in Week 7, but then got a well-timed bye week to recover. He was a full participant in Friday’s practice before being removed from the injury report entirely. Per usual, he will be near the top of the RB1 ranks for his date with the Raiders.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Tee Higgins caught 5-of-6 targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in the Bengals’ Week 9 victory over the Falcons.
item.description:
Tee Higgins CIN Wide Receiver

Higgins had recorded at least 148 receiving yards in three of his last four games. His 32 yards were a far cry from those gaudy totals, but he was able to save the day from a fantasy perspective by catching a four-yard touchdown and an eight-yard touchdown. Higgins still has 758 receiving yards on the season to Ja’Marr Chase’s 647, so he has that going for him. Higgins is technically the WR2 on the Bengals, but he’s a top-10 WR in fantasy heading into a matchup with the Steelers in Week 10.

item.title: Ja’Marr Chase caught 10-of-12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in the Bengals’ Week 9 win over the Falcons.
item.description:
Ja'Marr Chase CIN Wide Receiver

Chase hadn’t had a game with 100 yards receiving until two weeks ago. Since then, he’s had at least 10 receptions, at least 141 yards and a touchdown in back-to-back games. Ho-hum. Chase absolutely toasted Falcons cornerback AJ Terrell for a 47-yard touchdown in the first quarter on a play that looked eerily similar to a touchdown he had against Terrell when the two were in college. Chase is up to 647 yards and seven touchdowns on the season. He’s a WR1 heading into Week 10’s matchup against the Steelers.

item.title: Joe Burrow completed 24-of-29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in the Bengals’ 34-17 Week 9 win over the Falcons, adding three carries for seven yards and a touchdown.
item.description:
Joe Burrow CIN Quarterback

Burrow’s excellent run of play continued against the Falcons defense in Madrid in Week 9. The 29-year-old signal caller has amassed 16 passing touchdowns in the last four weeks and added two more touchdowns on the ground. Burrow’s production is unsurprisingly coming from playing through his top wide receivers as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins combined for 187 yards receiving and all three receiving touchdowns against Atlanta. Burrow is likely to find himself on the shortlist for the MVP award the way things are going. He’s a locked in QB1 heading into a Week 10 matchup with the Steelers on Sunday Night Football, which airs on NBC and Peacock.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is active for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson managed to draw a questionable tag entering the weekend after logging a limited practice on Friday. Despite being a DNP for two of the Rams’ three practices this week, he should be available to play his normal role in the Rams’ TE-heavy scheme. Parkinson has caught 14 passes for 103 yards and one touchdown this season and will not be on the fantasy radar this week. The Rams declared QB Ty Simpson, LS Joe Cardona, LB Darryl Peterson III, OL Bill Murray, OL Keagan Trost, and LB Desjuan Johnson inactive for Week 9.

item.title: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is active for Week 9 against the Browns.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

Tyson will make his NFL debut after missing the first two months of the year with a hamstring injury. We’re expecting a snap count for him this week, making him an extremely risky FLEX play. Inactive for the Saints are QB Zach Wilson, S Mike Reid, RB C.J. Donaldson, DT Christen Miller, LB Jaylan Ford, OL Mason Murphy, and DL John Ridgeway III.

item.title: Eagles declared WR DeVonta Smith, WR Dontayvion Wicks, LB Jihaad Campbell, CB Jonathan Jones, S Michael Carter II and WR Britain Covey inactive for Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

Smith has now been active just one time since Week 3. With the Eagles no longer particularly interested in the 2026 season, we would consider Smith no better than 50-50 to return following the team’s Week 10 bye.

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Mike Evans (Achilles) is “questionable at best” for Week 10 against the Cowboys.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

The 49ers bungled Christian McCaffrey’s Achilles tendinitis in 2024 and are determined to get it right this time around with Evans. That means taking an extra cautious approach with his return to the field. He’s already been ruled out for Week 9 and now Week 10 sounds like a long-shot. Demarcus Robinson, who returned from injured reserve earlier this week, is somehow the team’s WR1 for today’s game against the Raiders.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: NFL insider Josina Anderson reports the Giants “cooled on acquiring Colts RB Jonathan Taylor because of price.”
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

She added that the Giants have resolved to move on from the trade talks ahead of their Week 9 date with the Eagles. Things change quickly in the NFL and this report doesn’t guarantee that Taylor won’t be a Giant. On the other hand, Anderson’s reporting doesn’t leave much room error. With the Colts’ asking price reportedly being through the roof, the Giants are content with Cam Skattebo as their top back. Devin Singletary is expected to start this week with Skattebo banged up.

Source: Josina Anderson

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Deshaun Watson cleared the league’s concussion protocol but will be inactive for Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Watson returned to practice on Friday for a limited session and cleared the league’s protocol over the weekend. Still, after preparing Shedeur Sanders to start throughout the week, head coach Todd Monken decided not to throw a curveball at his own team on game day. Sanders will start and Dillon Gabriel will back him up. Watson has rebounded this year, but the lows are still staggeringly low. He took eight sacks in a blowout loss to the Steelers last week. If Sanders plays well today, Monken will at least have something to think about ahead of Week 10.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) will not play in Week 9 against the Bucs.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

Per Rapoport, Monangai is expected to return after Chicago’s Week 10 bye. Monangai has been out since Week 4. He finally returned to practice earlier this week, but it was for a single, limited session on Friday. He should be back in a 1B role when the Bears take on the Saints in two weeks.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

St. Brown was limited in practice throughout the week. He has a knack for getting it out through injuries and will do so again today. Even at less than full strength, St. Brown shouldn’t face much resistance from Miami’s weak secondary. He remains a top-end WR1 for his Week 9 game in South Beach.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Emeka Egbuka (foot) will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka missed two games with the foot injury, though a concussion also kept him out for one of them. He practiced in full on Friday, so we’re not expecting much of a pitch count for the second-year wideout. Without anyone emerging as a viable replacement for Egbuka over the past two weeks, he should reclaim the No. 1 receiver role in Tampa Bay without much of a fight. Egbuka will be on the WR2/3 border for his first game back.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Bengals declared S Kyle Dugger, C Connor Lew, OT Myles Hinton, and DT Landon Robinson inactive for Week 9 against the Falcons.
item.description:
Kyle Dugger CIN Safety

The Bengals are surprisingly healthy headed into their date with the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. Dugger is the only one of their inactives who is out with an injury. The rest are healthy scratches.

item.title: Falcons EDGE James Pearce Jr. (back) is active for Week 9 against the Bengals.
item.description:
James Pearce ATL Defensive End

Pearce Jr. just finished serving his eight-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy. A back issue then flared up in practice, but he’s good to go for his 2026 debut. Inactive for the Falcons are QB Andy Dalton, QB Jack Strand, WR Zachariach Branch, DB Billy Bowman, DB Robert Longerbeam, and DE Drake Jackson.

item.title: Falcons placed RB Brian Robinson (hamstring) on injured reserve.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

The timing of the transaction is curious after Robinson missed the previous two games with the injury, potentially signaling a setback in his recovery. Either way, Robinson will now miss the coming four games, at minimum, leaving Bijan Robinson in a clear workhorse role in the immediate future.

item.title: Broncos activated WR Pat Bryant (ankle) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

The young receiver will make his return to the active game-day roster after missing the minimum four games after injuring his ankle in Week 4. He returns to a passing attack with no clear direction or upside, with no receiver other than Courtland Sutton playing in a near every-down role of late. Perhaps he can carve out a featured role, but it is more likely this team simply doesn’t have viable weekly fantasy assets through the air.

item.title: 49ers activated WR Demarcus Robinson (ankle) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Demarcus Robinson SF Wide Receiver

The veteran receiver returns to a decimated receiving corps, potentially in line to serve as the top receiver against the Raiders in Week 9. Fantasy managers in a bind could do much worse than taking a swing on Robinson considering the elite matchup and lack of viable depth, for a 49ers team with one of the week’s highest Vegas implied team totals on the board.

item.title: Vikings ruled out Jauan Jennings (calf) for Week 9 against the Bills.
item.description:
Jauan Jennings MIN Wide Receiver

The fantasy implications of Jennings’ absence are negligible, with the bigger boost to the passing offense being the absence of Kyler Murray, who is looking at a multi-game absence with a Grade 2 hamstring injury. Tai Felton appears to be in line for additional run as the team’s WR3, although he is not a recommended streaming option with both Jefferson and Jordan Addison healthy.

item.title: Vikings ruled out Kyler Murray (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Bills.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

Murray will likely be sidelined for multiple games after testing revealed a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Carson Wentz will draw the start under center while the team is reportedly exploring the trade market ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. The absence of Murray should benefit alpha wide receiver Justin Jefferson, who has struggled to develop chemistry with Murray this season.

item.title: Dion Dawkins (ribs) and Alec Anderson (ankle) are questionable for Week 9 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Dion Dawkins BUF Tackle

The Bills enter Week 9 with the entire left side of one the league’s top offensive lines questionable. Both players did not practice through Friday before drawing the questionable tag for Monday Night Football against the Vikings. We likely won’t know their respective statuses until inactives are released 90 minutes prior to first kick. Absences would be a detriment to the run game and could lead to increased emphasis on the short areas of the field through the air.

item.title: Bills ruled out Joshua Palmer (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Vikings.
item.description:
Joshua Palmer BUF Wide Receiver

Palmer has been in and out of the lineup since injuring his hamstring in Week 4, managing only seven offensive snaps last week before succumbing to an aggravation. He will miss his second game of the season when the Bills take on the one-loss Vikings on Monday Night Football. Skylar Bell could find himself active for the third time in his rookie season, although DJ Moore, Keon Coleman, and Khalil Shakir are likely to dominate snaps and routes at the position.

item.title: Saints released RB Kendre Miller.
item.description:
Kendre Miller

The team brought back Audric Estime to their practice squad earlier in the week, releasing Miller Saturday. The moved comes after the veteran played 137 offensive snaps for a backfield missing its top option for most of the season. Miller had a 20-carry game for the Saints three short weeks ago and now finds himself without a home. Expect him to land on a practice squad in short order.

Source: Nick Underhill

item.title: NFL Insider Jordan Schultz reports Saints WR Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) “should be good to go” against the Browns in Week 9.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

The oft-injured Tyson hurt his hamstring in training camp and is yet to make his NFL debut. According to Schultz, he should be good to go Sunday against the Browns. A limited participant in practice throughout the week, it’s unclear how much Tyson might play in his first game. Eventually, though, he should settle in as the Saints’ WR2 behind Chris Olave. Tyson’s return also puts a damper on the fantasy prospects of Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Rams activated EDGE Myles Garrett (knee) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

No surprise here as Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Garrett is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders. The Rams are 4-4, but will finally have Garrett and Aaron Donald on the same defensive line. That could cause problems for opposing offensive lines, starting with Washington’s on Sunday.

Source: Rams

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Seahawks QB Drew Lock (elbow) has severe tendonitis in his elbow.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Pelissero reiterated that Lock looked good in practice and will start against the Cardinals in Week 9. Still, Lock has been dealing with this since earlier this season and at one point wasn’t able to throw because of it. Seahawks HC Mike Macdonald said earlier this week he didn’t know how much Lock will be able to throw. Despite his play in relief of Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) earlier this year, Lock isn’t a priority in 1QB leagues. Jalen Milroe could even be worth stashing in deeper formats given that Lock’s tendonitis could flare up at anytime.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: NFL reporter Aaron Wilson reports RB Dameon Pierce (hamstring) is drawing interest from multiple teams.
item.description:
Dameon Pierce

Pierce was released by the Eagles after agreeing to an injury settlement on Friday. He’s currently still dealing with what Wilson described as a “relatively minor” hamstring injury. Wilson lists the Dolphins, Jaguars, Panthers, Ravens, 49ers, Cardinals and Titans as teams that have contracted Pierce, who is rehabbing in Houston. Expected to be ready in 2-3 weeks, Pierce could catch on with another team soon, though it’s unlikely to be in a starting role.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Titans WR Calvin Ridley “could be had for a late-round pick.”
item.description:
Calvin Ridley TEN Wide Receiver

The Titans are listening on Ridley, who could be had for a late-round pick, according to Schefter. The Chiefs, Steelers and 49ers are the most likely teams to be in the market for a wide receiver ahead of Tuesday’s trade deadline. The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero also reported that multiple wide receivers could be traded before the deadline and listed Ridley as a name to watch.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Titans aren’t interested in trading RB Tony Pollard.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

A previous report from Albert Breer suggested the team might be willing to trade Pollard, who is in the last year of his contract, for a fourth-round pick. Schefter threw cold water on that theory, reporting Tennessee isn’t interested in trading the 29-year-old running back. Showing fresh legs in recent weeks, Pollard is a solid RB2 the rest of the way even on a struggling Titans offense.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Commanders “haven’t completely abandoned” the idea of acquiring WR Brandon Aiyuk.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk SF Wide Receiver

Aiyuk was rumored to end up in Washington all offseason and there seemingly could still be a fit there with Terry McLaurin out for the season. However, this report suggests the Commanders haven’t completely ruled it out rather than this being something they’re actively pursuing. Aiyuk met with 49ers brass Friday, though a resolution proved elusive. This saga is far from over.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have told teams they’ve received an offer of a fourth-round pick for WR Josh Downs.
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

The Colts’ original asking price for Downs, who has requested a trade, was a third-round pick. Indianapolis has told teams they already have an offer of a fourth-round pick for the 25-year-old receiver, who is in the last year of his rookie contract. Downs is probably one of the more likelier players to be traded ahead of the deadline. Teams have also called the Colts about Keenan Allen, though he’s unlikely to bring back a similar trade return given his age.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Chargers have no interest in trading EDGE Khalil Mack.
item.description:
Khalil Mack LAC Outside Linebacker

Despite the Chargers being 0-7, Los Angeles isn’t acting like it. Mack is 35, on an expiring contract and seeming could garner an early day-three pick in a trade. Still, the Chargers are content to keep Mack, who Schefter says won’t be going anywhere prior to the trade deadline.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Broncos checked on Trey McBride.
item.description:
Trey McBride ARI Tight End

To no one’s surprise, the Cardinals hung up the phone in record time. Even as a perennially rebuilding franchise, Arizona was never going to trade arguably the league’s best tight end in the middle of his prime. Schefter added that the Cardinals have “checked in around the league on tight ends.” Evan Engram has a measly 13 catches for 136 yards this year and Denver’s passing attack has taken a step back despite acquiring Jaylen Waddle in the offseason. Dallas Goedert is the biggest name believed to be available at tight end ahead of Tuesday’s deadline. On an expiring contract, he wouldn’t cost the Broncos much. Carolina tight end Ja’Tavion Sanders is likely on the trade block as well.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: The Athletic’s Jonathan Jones reports the Jets have no desire or intention to trade RB Breece Hall.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

While the Jets traded young players for draft picks last season, don’t expect New York to do that again this year. A team source told Jones the Jets moving Hall is “very unlikely to happen.” Hall appears ready to return from a quad injury in Week 9 against the Chiefs, but is difficult to trust in fantasy with Braelon Allen potentially cutting into his workload after a strong showing in Hall’s absence in recent weeks.

Source: Jonathan Jones

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Vikings QB Kyler Murray has a Grade 2 hamstring strain.
item.description:
Kyler Murray MIN Quarterback

Previous reports said Murray was “week-to-week” with the injury. There’s no question the Vikings will monitor Murray’s health every week, but a Grade 2 hamstring strain typically leads to missing multiple games. With Carson Wentz set to start on Monday Night Football against the Bills in Week 9 and the Vikings monitoring outside QB options ahead of the trade deadline, Murray isn’t even guaranteed to be the starter again once he’s healthy.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Lamar Jackson is out for 6-9 weeks with a fractured and dislocated thumb.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Per Rapoport, Jackson has already told his teammates he plans to return this season. While even the short end of that timeline would only have Jackson back in Week 15, it’s an optimistic turn of events for a quarterback who was previously expected to miss the rest of the season. At a nine-week return, Jackson would need Baltimore to make the playoffs to have a shot at returning this year. Jacoby Brissett will likely close out the fantasy season as Baltimore’s starting quarterback, but there’s a chance we get Jackson back for a final game or two in the regular season.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Patriots activated WR Mack Hollins (calf) from injured reserve.
item.description:
Mack Hollins NE Wide Receiver

Hollins misses the minimum four games with a calf injury and returns to a pass catching corps without A.J. Brown and TreVeyon Henderson, while tight end Hunter Henry is also listed as questionable for Week 9. There is opportunity for him to lead the team in receiving with the bulk of the remaining healthy players largely operating in the short-to-intermediate areas of the field. Fantasy managers in a bid could do worse as a FLEX option against the Packers.

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports the Colts have told teams they aren’t trading QB Daniel Jones.
item.description:
Daniel Jones IND Quarterback

Despite ESPN’s Adam Schefter trying to will a Jones trade into existence by recreating Brian Windhorst memes, Pelissero reports the Colts have informed teams they aren’t trading the 29-year-old quarterback. Jones is set to start against the Cowboys in Week 9, but could find himself on the bench once the Colts are eliminated from playoff contention given the injury guarantees for next season in his contract.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Colts RB Jonathan Taylor “most likely” won’t be traded.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

An earlier report from the Athletic’s Jonathan Jones listed the Vikings and Giants as the favorites to trade for Taylor while the Seahawks, Packers and Broncos are still in the mix. Pelissero threw cold water on all of that by reporting no team has come close to offering what the Colts want for Taylor. Maybe that changes after Week 9, but if Taylor is stuck in Indianapolis, that’s probably the worst-case scenario for his rest-of-season fantasy value.

Source: Tom Peliserro

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Colts have received calls from multiple teams about trading for QB Daniel Jones.
item.description:
Daniel Jones IND Quarterback

Schefter passes along that the Ravens called the Colts about Jones before they acquired Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals. Otherwise, this report lacked specifics. According to league sources, multiple teams have called the Colts about trading for Jones, but he couldn’t name a team other than the Ravens. Schefter mentions the Vikings as a possibility, but while that suggestion makes sense given Minnesota’s need at quarterback and Jones’ history with the organization, it’s still purely speculation at this point. Jones is set to start against the Cowboys in Week 9, but isn’t on the fantasy radar outside of 2QB/superflex leagues.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Giants inquired about Ravens RB Justice Hill.
item.description:
Justice Hill BAL Running Back

Schefter reports that Hill rather than Derrick Henry was the running back the Giants called the Ravens about. While Henry is certainly the better back between the two, Schefter also reported that the Ravens won’t trade him. With Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful and Tyrone Tracey on injured reserve, the Giants are looking for help in the backfield. Hill would help in that regard, but until a trade is consummated, he doesn’t have much standalone fantasy value behind Henry in Baltimore.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports the Ravens aren’t expected to trade RB Derrick Henry.
item.description:
Derrick Henry BAL Running Back

Citing league sources, Schefter says the Ravens recently informed Henry that they have no intention of trading him. While speculation about a trade is understandable given Baltimore’s injuries at the quarterback position, the Ravens are said to have never even considered it, according to Schefter. With the newly acquired Jacoby Brissett likely to be under center in Week 10 against the Chargers, Henry will be in the RB1 mix.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that the Chargers “still do not appear eager to sell players” ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
item.description:
Khalil Mack LAC Outside Linebacker

Fowler said he spoke to multiple executives around the league this week, and the general sentiment is that the Chargers are not interested in making any moves. Fowler wonders aloud whether Khalil Mack, who has generated “a lot of interest,” could be had for a fourth- or fifth-round pick. Mack, 35, certainly makes sense for contending teams. The 0-7 Chargers do not qualify as such.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Daniel Jones “maybe wants to” be traded away from the Colts.
item.description:
Daniel Jones IND Quarterback

Fowler says that multiple sources around the league, including multiple sources inside the Colts’ organization, believe Jones “should be trying to get out of Indy, or maybe wants to.” The Colts are entering a rebuild, with trade rumors swirling around multiple star players. Fowler closed the segment by hinting at the Vikings as a possible landing spot. Jones’ fantasy-scoring outlook might tick up a little bit were he to head back to Minnesota.

Source: Jeremy Fowler

item.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports that Jordan Elliott will work out for the Bears next week.
item.description:
Jordan Elliott

Elliott was released by the Titans a couple of weeks ago due to an “incident” at their facility. Schultz says that Titans coach Robert Saleh has been an “advocate” for Elliott despite the team releasing him. Should they bring him aboard, the Bears would further solidify their interior defensive line after recently acquiring Jeffery Simmons.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Brandon Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said talks between him and the 49ers are “to be continued.”
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk SF Wide Receiver

Aiyuk and Rosenhaus met with the 49ers’ “big bosses” today to discuss an amicable solution to their multi-year conflict. Aiyuk seeks reinstatement, but under league rules, he

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Kenny Gainwell (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Gainwell has been a little more involved in recent weeks, and coach Todd Bowles recently told reporters that they are getting closer to the 1A/1B usage that they envisioned when they signed him. Gainwell will again play sidekick to Bucky Irving this week.

Source: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

item.title: Tristan Wirfs (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
item.description:
Tristan Wirfs TB Tackle

The Buccaneers will have their starting left tackle on hand when they take on the Bears’ ascending defensive line in Week 9. Wirfs is one of the best offensive tackles in football. Having him on the field is always a plus for Baker Mayfield.

Source: Tampa Bay Buccaneers

item.title: George Pickens (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Colts.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Earlier today, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is “hopeful” that Pickens will be available for this weekend’s game against the Colts. Pickens ended up being limited in practice all week and appears to be truly questionable to play. If active, he is a WR2 against a beatable Colts defense.

Source: Dallas Cowboys

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
item.description:
Rashee Rice KC Wide Receiver

Rice posted a 7/53/1 receiving line against the Broncos last week. He got in a limited session on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. He seems to be recovering effectively from his summer knee procedure and in-season hamstring injury. Rice is a borderline WR1/2 for this weekend’s game against the Jets.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
item.description:
Travis Kelce KC Tight End

Kelce caught 5-of-7 targets for 67 yards, playing through the ankle injury last week against the Broncos, looking slightly hobbled. Kelce was limited to begin the week, but got in two full practices over the last two days. He remains firmly in the TE1 tier for Week 9 against the Jets.

Source: Kansas City Chiefs

item.title: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
item.description:
Christian Darrisaw MIN Tackle

Darrisaw is now firmly on track to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills, who field a tough, talented defensive line. Having Darrisaw on the field will be helpful for pocket passer Carson Wentz.

Source: Minnesota Vikings

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that “the plan” is for Quenton Nelson to avoid injured reserve after undergoing a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee.
item.description:
Quenton Nelson SEA Guard

If the Seahawks were to place Nelson on short-term injured reserve, he would be required to miss at least four games. The Seahawks face the Cardinals this week, the Raiders next and then go on bye. Nelson could have a chance to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. His availability that week will likely just come down to how the recovery is going. His loss is unfortunate.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

Wilson caught 8-of-15 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys while playing through a pair of broken ribs. The Cardinals kept him limited all week. He should be good to go for WR2 duties against the Seahawks’ elite defense this week.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: Commanders ruled out Treylon Burks (foot) for Week 9 against the Rams.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

The Commanders’ wide receiver corps continues to lose players. Burks and Dyami Brown (calf) will both be sidelined this weekend, leaving Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Chig Okonkwo to operate as the top pass catchers.

Source: Nicki Jhabvala

item.title: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Talanoa Hufanga DEN Safety

The Broncos’ talented safety might need another week to get his ankle healthy. Hufanga only logged two limited practice sessions this week. He has been sidelined since mid-October.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Pat Bryant (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

Bryant is expected to be activated from injured reserve by Saturday, but the team has officially listed him as questionable. He makes for a boom-bust FLEX in his first game back. The Broncos’ passing offense has struggled this season. Perhaps Bryant’s return lifts it up.

Source: Chris Tomasson

item.title: Dion Dawkins (ribs) did not practice on Friday.
item.description:
Dion Dawkins BUF Tackle

Dawkins and starting LG Alec Anderson (ankle) have now missed two practices this week. This is concerning. The Bills face the Vikings’ elite, blitz-based defense in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game. Hopefully, the extra day off helps them return in time.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Keon Coleman (shoulder) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
Keon Coleman BUF Wide Receiver

Coleman’s fantasy-scoring outlook has been hurt by his teammate’s improving health. At this point, Coleman is more so a single-game DFS FLEX rather than a starter in 12-team re-draft formats. He should be good to go for Week 9’s Monday Night Football game though.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: DJ Moore (shoulder) was limited on Friday.
item.description:
DJ Moore BUF Wide Receiver

The Bills are managing Moore’s AC joint sprain fairly well. He should be expected to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Vikings. Although it is a tough matchup, Moore remains the WR2 tier in this week’s final game.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: Dalton Kincaid (chest) practiced in full on Friday.
item.description:
Dalton Kincaid BUF Tight End

Kincaid remained limited in all three practices last week, so today’s return to full participation is great to see. The Vikings’ blitz-based defense often requires tight ends to stay in line to block, which could hurt Kincaid’s route volume. Regardless, he is too talented to be removed from the TE1 ranks.

Source: Buffalo Bills

item.title: David Njoku (fibula) is doubtful to play in Week 9 against the Texans.
item.description:
David Njoku LAC Tight End

Njoku was limited all week, though he apparently is not ready to return from injured reserve. He does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. The Chargers will likely employ a three-player rotation whenever he returns.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Texans ruled out Reed Blankenship (consussion/hand) for Week 9 against the Chargers.
item.description:
Reed Blankenship HOU Safety

The Texans will be without Blankenship this week, but they get Jalen Pitre (shoulder) back. The Texans’ defense has underperformed this year, as has the Chargers’ offense. Perhaps one of the units can facilitate a get-right outing for the other.

Source: Houston Texans

item.title: 49ers ruled out Christian Kirk (knee) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

At this point, Kirk probably does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues. He returned from his lengthy calf injury only to injure his knee. It’s a tough break for the veteran wide receiver.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Demarcus Robinson (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Demarcus Robinson SF Wide Receiver

If Robinson can make his return from injured reserve with Mike Evans (Achilles), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee) sidelined, Robinson could end up returning WR3 value against the Raiders this week. Wide receiver-needy fantasy managers should add him now.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: 49ers ruled out Deebo Samuel (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Samuel, Mike Evans (Achilles) and Christian Kirk (knee) are all sidelined, potentially leaving Demarcus Robinson (ankle) as a featured receiver if he can play. Samuel can continue to be stashed on benches in 12-team leagues, though his return timeline remains somewhat opaque.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: 49ers ruled out Mike Evans (Achilles) for Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans is dealing with tendinitis in his Achilles tendon that initially cropped up in Week 6. When speaking with the media earlier this week, general manager John Lynch said the team hopes to get Evans back in the “coming weeks,” which means he should tentatively be considered questionable to play in Week 10 against the Cowboys.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Nick Bosa (calf/knee) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive Lineman

Bosa strained his calf while going through his pre-practice warm-up routine before Week 3’s Thursday practice, and has not played since. He has also dealt with knee tendinitis. Bosa is finally cleared to return following the 49ers’ Week 8 bye.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Raiders.
item.description:
Christian McCaffrey SF Running Back

McCaffrey injured his hamstring in Week 7. The 49ers were on bye in Week 8, giving him extra time to rest. McCaffrey then sat out on Wednesday before practicing in a limited capacity on Thursday. He should be in fantasy football lineups this week, facing a soft Raiders run defense, but Kaelon Black could mix in for 8-10 touches, potentially warranting FLEX consideration.

Source: Matt Maiocco

item.title: Rams ruled out Terrance Ferguson (ankle/hamstring) for Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson was set to make his return from injured reserve, having rehabilitated his early-season ankle injury. Unfortunately, he strained his hamstring in practice today and has now been ruled out. With Colby Parkinson (ribs) questionable, Tyler Higbee sneaks back into the TE1 conversation.

Source: Dan Graziano

item.title: Drew Lock (elbow) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Lock has dealt with an injury in his throwing-arm elbow for multiple weeks. He was limited at each Week 9 practice, but told reporters that he was feeling good late on Wednesday. It is tough to say whether this will impact him on game day, but he warrants QB2 treatment against the Cardinals’ soft defense.

Source: John P. Boyle

item.title: Seahawks ruled out Rashid Shaheed (knee) for Week 9 against the Cardinals.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

The Seahawks will again be without their speedy, underused wide receiver. Fortunately, Tory Horton (hand) was removed from the injury report and will play this week. He will catch passes thrown by Drew Lock (elbow).

Source: John P. Boyle

item.title: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Quenton Nelson (knee) will have a minor procedure and is week-to-week.
item.description:
Quenton Nelson SEA Guard

Apparently, Nelson was dealing with this knee issue when Seattle acquired for him, and he recently “aggravated it to some degree.” FOX 59’s Mike Chappell notes that Nelson was never listed on the Colts’ injury report this season. This is a bummer for the Seahawks, who acquired Nelson as a win-now move. Nelson will not play in Week 9 against the Cardinals, and the Seahawks also ruled out LT Charles Cross (ankle), DT Leonard Williams (stinger) and LB Uchenna Nwosu (ankle).

Source: Mike Chappell

item.title: Mason Taylor (back) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Mason Taylor NYJ Tight End

Taylor’s contributions are far too volatile for him to be trusted in 12-team formats, but his presence hurts rookie TE Kenyon Sadiq’s fantasy-scoring outlook. Taylor does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Sione Vaki (ankle) is questionable for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Sione Vaki DET Running Back

Vaki and Lions RB3 Jacob Saylors (neck) are both questionable. Vaki did not practice on Friday, having apparently suffered a new injury. Saylors was limited all week. Jahmyr Gibbs should handle his normal, sizable workload.

Source: Detroit Lions

item.title: Lions ruled out Cade Mays (ankle) for Week 9 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Cade Mays DET Center

Brutal. Mays returned from injured reserve in Week 7 due to a preseason wrist injury. He injured his ankle in Week 8. The Lions ruled out S Kerby Joseph (knee) and CB D.J. Reed (hip), yet S Brian Branch (concussion) will play.

Source: Detroit Lions

item.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Dolphins.
item.description:
Amon-Ra St. Brown DET Wide Receiver

St. Brown rarely misses games due to injuries. Fantasy managers should remain optimistic about his availability. The Lions’ No. 1 wide receiver remained limited all week. Although it might hurt to take hits, we expect St. Brown to suit up this weekend. Regardless, keeping it locked to Rotoworld is a must. Updates will be provided as they roll in.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Jaylen Wright (quad) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Lions.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

Wright and Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) are both questionable in this one, though Allen upgraded to full participation on Friday while Wright remained limited. Wright is barely worthy of stashing in 12-team leagues.

Source: David Furones

item.title: Panthers ruled out Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Jaelan Phillips CAR Outside Linebacker

Phillips did not practice at all this week, after sitting out the Panthers’ last two games. Losing a key edge rusher will make things harder for the Panthers’ defense. Bo Nix should have decently comfortable pockets, though.

Source: Alex Zietlow

item.title: Malik Nabers (knee) is not on the final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

The Giants have smartly limited Nabers’ practice participation levels at times this season, allowing him to play very well while returning from last year’s season-ending knee injury. Nabers belongs in fantasy football lineups in this divisional showdown, as usual.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is doubtful to play in Week 9 against the Eagles.
item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Giants coach John Harbaugh told reporters earlier this week that Skattebo is day-to-day. Unfortunately, Skattebo only got in one limited session on Friday. Fantasy managers should expect Devin Singletary to get the start this week. He can be treated as a volume-based FLEX.

Source: Adam Caplan

item.title: Eagles ruled out Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) for Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
Jihaad Campbell PHI Linebacker

Campbell will now miss another game, beset by upper-leg injuries. The Eagles also ruled out DBs Michael Carter (abdomen) and Jonathan Jones (hamstring). The Eagles still have talented players available, but the defense is a little banged up.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Jake Elliott (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
Jake Elliott PHI Kicker

The Eagles’ kicker practiced in full today, which was good to see. Given the state of the Eagles’ offense, he may not have many field goal attempts this week, though. Kickers tend to benefit from playing on teams with stellar offenses. The Eagles no longer have one.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Eagles ruled out Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) for Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
Dontayvion Wicks PHI Wide Receiver

Wicks and DeVonta Smith (hamstring) will both miss this weekend’s game, before taking the week off next week as well. The Eagles go on bye in Week 10. Hopefully, the added rest will allow Wicks to be healthy down the stretch.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley will again play through his hamstring and back injuries. Touchdowns have helped offset Barkley’s moderate yardage totals, and the offense will now be led by Joe Milton. Barkley’s role and talent keep him in the high-end RB2 tier, though an apex outcome is perhaps unlikely, given the state of the Eagles’ offense.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

item.title: DeVonta Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Giants.
item.description:
DeVonta Smith PHI Wide Receiver

As expected, Smith will miss another week after not being able to practice due to his ankle troubles. The 27-year-old wideout could be an option after the Week 10 bye, but nothing is certain. The Eagles’ passing attack should be completely avoided for their divisional showdown with New York.

Source: Philadelphia Eagles

Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

Kamara was limited due to rest and a back injury, but unsurprisingly, he’ll be good to go for Sunday’s contest against the Browns. The Saints’ run game is a disaster, but Kamara should be involved enough in the pass game to make him a decent FLEX play for that contest.

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the NFL’s defensive tackle market “has been hot,” and teams “might” try to trade for Derrick Brown.
item.description:
Derrick Brown CAR Defensive Tackle

The Panthers are “not actively looking to move” Brown, but Breer says they have considered it. Other defensive tackles on other teams who have come up in trade talks include Grover Stewart, Davon Godchaux, Nathan Shepherd, Christian Barmore and Bobby Brown. The Dolphins have told teams they are not interested in trading away Zach Sieler.

Source: Sports Illustrated

item.title: Jauan Jennings (calf) was not seen practicing on Friday.
item.description:
Jauan Jennings MIN Wide Receiver

Jennings was limited yesterday, which could mean he injured his calf during the Vikings’ Thursday practice. If this is the case, he is probably unlikely to suit up for his team’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills.

Source: Alec Lewis

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that Josh Downs “leads the wide receiver market” ahead of the NFL trade deadline.
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

Downs’ 2026 season has fallen short of expectations, but perhaps he has a chance to rebound. Breer believes acquiring Downs would “probably” cost a fourth-round pick. He is “one of a number of receivers on the market” at the moment, with the Chiefs and Steelers among the teams looking for help at the position. Breer adds that the 49ers are “open” to adding a wide receiver as well, but with their positional health improving, San Francisco is “less desperate than they were a couple of weeks ago.” The Steelers’ wide receiver corps might be too muddled for Downs to meaningfully increase his productivity, but landing in Kansas City or San Francisco would likely be good for him.

Source: Sports Illustrated

item.title: Emeka Egbuka (foot) is listed as questionable for Week 9 against the Bears.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka was able to get in another full practice Friday after getting the same Thursday, so it seems like he’s on the right side of the questionable tag, even with coach Todd Bowles suggesting he’ll be a game-time decision. The 24-year-old wideout is on the WR2/WR3 range for the Sunday Night Football showdown against Chicago if he is able to go.

Source: Rick Stroud

item.title: Denzel Boston (calf) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

Boston will once again play through a lower-body injury. The rookie downfield wide receiver has played unproductively as of late, but he remains a threat to rip off a long gain. He will be catching passes from Shedeur Sanders this weekend. Hopefully, the two form a strong connection quickly.

Source: Cleveland Browns

item.title: KaVontae Turpin (ribs) was ruled out for Week 9 against the Colts.
item.description:
KaVontae Turpin DAL Wide Receiver

This will be a third-straight missed game for Turpin as he battles his rib issue. The 30-year-old has just seven targets on the season, but will again be missed by Dallas in the return game. Malachi Lawrence has also been ruled out by the Cowboys due to his ankle injury.

Source: Calvin Watkins

item.description:
Jake Ferguson DAL Tight End

Ferguson wasn’t able to practice Wednesday or Thursday, but he was able to get in a limited session Friday to give him at least a chance to play Friday. Luke Schoonmaker (groin) was also listed as questionable with limited practices all week. If Ferguson is able to play, he’s in the TE2 vicinity against Indianapolis.

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Jaguars “have been less inclined” to trade away Brian Thomas.
item.description:
Brian Thomas

Breer and NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe put out similar reports today, indicating that the Jaguars are now hesitant to trade away Thomas. Per Breer, Thomas is not the best fit for coach Liam Coen’s scheme, but he “brings a downfield element that’s really important in keeping defenses honest against the run, and opening things up underneath for Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington.” Wolfe echoed Breer’s downfield sentiment and added that when the Jaguars traded away Tyson Campbell last year, it had a negative impact on the locker room — and Jaguars brass has “learned from it.” Thomas and Travis Hunter are reportedly close friends, and Thomas is liked in the locker room. It sounds like the formerly productive wide receiver might be staying put. Breer lists the Chiefs and Steelers, and the 49ers to a lesser degree, as the teams known to be seeking wide receiver help.

Source: Sports Illustrated

item.title: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) returned to practice Friday.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

The Bears are calling the tailback questionable for Week 9 against the Buccaneers. It’s the first time that Monangai has been able to practice picking up the injury a month ago against the Jets. It seems extremely unlikely that the 24-year-old will be able to play against Tampa Bay on Sunday night, but he appears to be on track to return after the Week 10 bye for the final stretch. Malik Muhammed and Tyrique Stevenson are also questionable for the Sunday Night showdown.

Source: Brad Biggs
