item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Giants are serious suitors for Jonathan Taylor, while the Broncos and Vikings might be less inclined to acquire him.
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

All three teams have inquired about Taylor’s trade cost. Per Breer, the Colts either want a first-round pick or a draft pick package similar to what the Panthers received for Christian McCaffrey in 2023. The 49ers handed over 2023 second-, third- and fourth-round picks, and a 2024 fifth-rounder to acquire him. None of the three suitors have met either asking price yet. That said, the Giants have reportedly offered enough for Breer to label them “a serious suitor.” Stay tuned.

Source: Sports Illustrated

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Parkinson sat out on Wednesday and Thursday. His Friday participation level has not yet been released, but he is probably on the wrong side of questionable at this time. Parkinson does not need to be rostered in 12-team leagues, especially with Terrance Ferguson (ankle) expected to play.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: Jordan Whittington (back) is questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Jordan Whittington

Whittington has just two catches on the season, and with head coach Sean McVay suggesting he wants to get Tutu Atwell more involved, it seems unlikely Whittington will have a role as more than a returner even if he can play against Washington come Sunday. Trent McDuffie (back) is also questionable for that contest, and won’t practice Friday.

Source: Nate Atkins

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Kelvin Banks (ankle) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Browns.
item.description:
Kelvin Banks NO Tackle

Banks, the Saints’ talented left tackle, has a chance to return from injured reserve this week. He underwent surgery earlier this year to address a high-ankle sprain. Banks’ backup, Asim Richards (thum), is also questionable to play. Hopefully, at least one of them is good to go.

Source: Kat Terrell

item.title: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters that Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 9 against the Commanders.
item.description:
Terrance Ferguson

Ferguson will be able to play for the first time since he suffered his medial ankle sprain in Week 3. The second-year tight end offers some volatility, but there’s no denying that there’s upside in his profile. Just don’t be shocked if it isn’t on full display just yet in Week 9.

Source: Sarah Barshop

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Rams HC Sean McVay told reporters Friday that Myles Garrett (knee) is expected to play against the Commanders in Week 9.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Garrett will need to come off injured reserve, with the Rams likely making that transaction closer to gametime. The 30-year-old has been as good as any defensive player in football, and for the first time he’ll get to be on the same field as Aaron Donald as teammates. Best of luck, Commanders’ offensive line.

Source: Sarah Barshop

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Browns.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

We do not yet know Tyson’s participation level at Friday’s practice, but he remained limited on Wednesday and Thursday. It seems like he may need another week before he makes his NFL debut, but we don’t know for sure. If active, Tyson would be FLEX-viable. It is possible the team initially keeps him on a snap count.

Source: Kat Terrell

item.title: CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Browns.
item.description:
CJ Donaldson NO Running Back

Donaldson wasn’t able to practice again Friday, and the 22-year-old tailback won’t be available for the Week 9 skirmish against Cleveland. Alvin Kamara will likely be the top option — and would have been even if Donaldson could play — in that contest, assuming his back injury allows him to play, of course. This is not a great situation, folks.

Source: Matthew Paras

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Deshaun Watson (concussion) will not start in Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Head coach Todd Monken said Watson will be questionable for Sunday’s game, but has already said Shedeur Sanders will make his first start of the season. Watson missed Wednesday’s and Thursday’s practices but was upgraded to a limited participant on Friday, although he has yet to clear concussion protocol. The decision to start Sanders likely stems from him working with the first-team offense during the week and the unlikelihood of Watson clearing protocol in time for Sunday’s game.

Source: Andrew Siciliano

item.title: Panthers head coach Dave Canales said Bryce Young (ankle) will play in Week 9 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Bryce Young CAR Quarterback

Young never really felt like he was at risk of missing this week. Despite dealing with an ankle injury, the Panthers’ QB1 was listed as a full participant in practice throughout the week and will be good to go despite what appears to be a minor ankle injury. Young draws a tough Week 9 matchup at home against the Broncos and has thrown two touchdowns and three interceptions in his last two games, and has completed below 60 percent of his passes in his last three outings. He’ll be a risky QB2 this week.

Source: Joe Person

item.title: A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Brown was unable to practice again Friday, and the 29-year-old will not be able to roll against the Green Bay secondary. It’s a second-consecutive missed game for Brown, who has played in just three games since his blockbuster deal to the Patriots prior to the season. DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams will be Drake Maye’s top wideout targets for the game against Green Bay. Not ideal.

Source: James Palmer

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said Bam Knight (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Seahawks.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

LaFleur also ruled out OL Jon Gaines II (ankle) and OT Jayden Williams (knee). Knight has been a DNP all week after suffering a concussion in Week 8’s win over the Cowboys and will officially be sidelined for Week 9. His absence, along with Jeremiyah Love’s (ankle) could create a bell cow role for Tyler Allgeier, who totaled 191 yards from scrimmage and two touchdowns in last week’s win, while fourth-year vet Evan Hull could also work into the mix. Allgeier’s volume alone will put him in the RB2 conversation this week despite the tough matchup.

Source: Josh Weinfuss

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Myles Garrett (knee) “is on track to be activated ahead of Sunday vs. the Commanders.”
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Garrett has practiced all week and will likely be activated in the next 24 to 48 hours. The star pass-rusher who was acquired by the Rams in a blockbuster trade this offseason played in just one game for the Rams this season and did not record a tackle. Now, after undergoing knee surgery to correct a nagging injury, Garrett is all but set to return against the Commanders after missing seven straight games. His return will provide a much-needed boost to a Rams defense that ranks near the bottom of the league in sacks (12) through the first half of the season.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Malik Nabers (knee) returned to practice on Friday.
item.description:
Malik Nabers NYG Wide Receiver

Nabers was a surprise DNP with a knee injury on Thursday, but said after practice that he expected to play. His return to the field on Friday suggests he will be good to go for Sunday’s game against the Eagles, but we will still check in with a final status when the Giants announce player designations for the weekend. Assuming he is good to go, Nabers should be treated as a normal must-start receiver against a down-bad Eagles team.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: DJ Turner (heel) will play in the Bengals’ Week 9 game against the Falcons.
item.description:
DJ Turner CIN Cornerback

After being upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice, Turner was officially removed from the injury report on Friday, meaning he will be good to go for Sunday’s international tilt against the Falcons. Turner has allowed 16 receptions for 133 yards and one touchdown on 26 targets this season, per PFF, earning a coverage grade of 72.9.

Source: Cincinnati Bengals

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Breece Hall (quad) will play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

This comes a day after Hall said he expects to play, so this news isn’t all too surprising. Hall’s return could somewhat complicate the Jets’ backfield situation on Sunday, however, as Braelon Allen has played well in Hall’s absence, making a strong case for more touches even when Hall is healthy. Glenn declined to get into how he plans to divvy up his running backs’ touches next week, saying “both guys will play,” when asked about his plans. This was already shaping up to be a tough fantasy matchup on the road against the Chiefs, but a potential backfield split would only further complicate matters. Until we see how things shake out, both Hall and Allen should be viewed as mid-to-low-end RB2s.

Source: Rich Cimini

item.title: Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley said Kadyn Proctor cleared concussion protocol and will play in Week 9 against the Lions.
item.description:
Kadyn Proctor MIA Offensive Lineman

Proctor missed last week’s game against the Patriots with a brain injury, but will be back in his normal left guard position for this week’s game against the Lions. In six games this season, Proctor has appeared on more than 350 offensive snaps, earning a PFF grade of 64.8 while allowing one sack and 13 pressures.

Source: Barry Jackson

item.title: The Ravens and Cardinals finalized a trade on Friday that sends Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore.
item.description:
Jacoby Brissett BAL Quarterback

We already knew this deal would be done, but the two sides made things official on Friday. The Ravens will receive Brissett, along with a 2027 fifth-round pick from the Cardinals in exchange for a 2027 4th-round pick and a 2028 7th-round pick. Brissett will immediately step into a starting role for the Ravens when they face the Chargers in Week 10 and should provide an immediate upgrade over Joe Fagnano, who struggled mightily in his first career start against the Jaguars.

item.title: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said Garrett Wilson (concussion) will not play in Week 9 against the Chiefs.
item.description:
Garrett Wilson NYJ Wide Receiver

Wilson has not practiced this week and has now been ruled out for Sunday’s game against the Chiefs. Wilson has caught 43 passes for 527 yards and three touchdowns this season and saw 12 targets in last week’s loss to the Raiders. His absence means both Adonai Mitchell and Omar Cooper should see expanded roles, but both players will be hard to trust as anything more than WR3s against a stout Chiefs defense. In addition to Wilson, the Jets also ruled out LB Trevin Wallace (groin) for Week 9.

Source: New York Jets

item.title: TreVeyon Henderson released a statement saying that he was dealing with an “unexpected and unusual medical emergency involving a series of unexplained neurological symptoms that required hospitalization for several days.”
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

This certainly sounds like a scary situation for Henderson, whose absence has been the subject of speculation for nearly two weeks. Henderson said that the results of “comprehensive medical testing have come back positive and reassuring, but he continues to work with specialists and physical therapists. Henderson said these issues have affected his “strength, coordination, and some of [his] physical functions,” while adding that he is working to return to full health. While we don’t want to speculate too much, it doesn’t sound like Henderson will be back anytime soon. Hopefully we will get more clarity on his situation soon, but our thoughts are with him and his continued recovery.

Source: TreVeyon Henderson

item.title: Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said he is “hopeful” George Pickens (hamstring) will play in Week 9 against the Colts.
item.description:
George Pickens DAL Wide Receiver

Pickens has been limited in each of the Cowboys’ first two practices to start the week, which would seem to be a good sign for his Week 9 availability. We’ll get a better sense of where things stand when the Cowboys release their final injury report on Friday and give Pickens a designation heading into the weekend, but Schottenheimer’s optimism is a good sign. Owner Jerry Jones advocated for Pickens getting the ball more this week after Week 8’s loss to the Cardinals, so if he is active, the star receiver could be primed for a bit of a squeaky wheel game in a plus matchup against the Colts.

Source: Tommy Yarrish

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Deshaun Watson (concussion) is “unlikely to start” in Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description:
Deshaun Watson CLE Quarterback

Watson has not practiced this week due to concussion symptoms he has been dealing with since Week 8’s loss to the Steelers. Unless he surprisingly clears concussion protocol this week, Watson will miss Week 9, paving the way for Shedeur Sanders to make his first start of the season. We will have official word on Watson’s status in a few hours, but at this point, it would be surprising if he does start.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: The Ringer’s Tom Pelissero reports Brandon Aiyuk owes the 49ers “roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture,” which could delay his return.
item.description:
Brandon Aiyuk SF Wide Receiver

Pelissero calls this a “potential complication in [Aiyuk’s] efforts to secure his release by reporting to the facility Friday.” While it’s possible both sides reach a deal for Aiyuk to pay back that money, which would make this a non-issue, Pelissero said this could also end up going to arbitration, which may delay things. Aiyuk is scheduled to report to the 49ers’ facilities today, so we could have our answer in the next few hours about when this situation is resolved and Aiyuk has been granted his release. Aiyuk recently hired Drew Rosenhaus with the hopes of being reinstated into the league and with a new team soon. The 28-year-old last played in 2024.

Source: Tom Pelissero

item.title: James Pearce is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Bengals.
item.description:
James Pearce ATL Defensive End

Pearce’s status is related to a back injury that apparently flared up in Friday’s practice, per head coach Kevin Stefanski. Pearce was a full participant in practice, and teams said he will operate on a pitch count, so it seems highly unlikely he will be scratched on game day. In addition to Pearce, the Falcons also listed LB Yasir Abdullah (hamstring), WR Beaux Collins (hip), LB Divine Deablo (forearm), and OT Cameron Williams (ankle) as questionable for Week 9.

Source: Atlanta Falcons

item.title: Brian Robinson (hamstring) is questionable for the Falcons’ Week 9 game against the Bengals.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

Robinson was briefly listed as questionable only for head coach Kevin Stefanski to rule him out shortly after the initial report. Robinson was limited in practice throughout the week, but the Falcons are opting to play it safe, likely hoping another week on the sidelines will lower the chances of re-injury. Rookie WR Zachariah Branch (hamstring) has also been ruled out for the game after picking up an injury in last week’s loss to the Buccaneers.

Source: Tori McElhaney

item.title: Mark Andrews caught both targets for 19 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Mark Andrews BAL Tight End

Andrews, somewhat disgustingly, led the team in receiving with a modest 19 yards on a night undrafted free agent rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano threw for only 60 yards in his first career start. It remains difficult to start the veteran tight end, who has made more mental mistakes this season than he has receptions.

item.title: Zay Flowers caught 3-of-6 targets for six yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 17 yards on three carries.
item.description:
Zay Flowers BAL Wide Receiver

Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did what he could to overcome undrafted free agent rookie Joe Fagnano under center, routinely putting Flowers in Motion across the formation to generate some level of misdirection for an offense with zero ability to attack downfield. That included three rush attempts and a completion thrown by running back Derrick Henry, but it wasn’t enough to salvage a usable fantasy week for the electric receiver. Fantasy managers can rest easy knowing help is on the way in the form of veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who was signed earlier in the week and will likely make his team debut when the Ravens take on the Chargers in Week 10. Flowers will return to upside WR2 range with the change at quarterback.

item.title: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Derrick Henry BAL Running Back

Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything in his power to overcome an undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first professional start, going so far as to call numerous direct snaps to Henry and a Henry pass attempt, but it ultimately proved futile. Things appeared to be trending in the right direction as the Ravens played the Jaguars to a tightly contested game through the first 29 minutes before Parker Washington broke the game open with a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the break. Things got nasty for Henry after the half as he managed only two additional yards after bruising his way to 55 first half yards. Henry will return to RB1 status in fantasy circles in Week 10 when the Ravens take on the Chargers.

item.title: Justice Hill rushed nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding seven yards on three receptions.
item.description:
Justice Hill BAL Running Back

Hill became the first running back to amass more than 75 yards against the Jaguars since the start of the 2025 regular season with a 65-yard touchdown with the game well out of hand in the second half. It was an otherwise poor showing for the entirety of the Baltimore offense with a rookie undrafted free agent starting his first NFL game. Hill remains nothing more than a desperation FLEX ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Chargers.

item.title: Browns head coach Todd Monken said Shedeur Sanders will start in Week 9 against the Saints.
item.description:
Shedeur Sanders CLE Quarterback

Sanders will draw the start as Deshaun Watson (concussion) has yet to clear protocol in time to be ready for Sunday’s game. Interestingly, Watson is still expected to be listed as questionable, per Monken, but Sanders will draw the start. We are assuming this decision is based on Sanders taking first-team reps after Watson missed each of the first two days of practice, but this is a nice opportunity for Sanders to show whatever growth he has made since a tough rookie season in which he threw for 1,440 yards, seven touchdowns, and 10 interceptions in eight games played. He’ll be on the low-end QB2 radar on the road against the Saints, who rank 16th in fantasy points allowed to opposing QBs this season.

Source: Andrew Siciliano

item.title: Hunter Henry (foot) has been ruled questionable for Week 9 against the Packers.
item.description:
Hunter Henry NE Tight End

The Patriots are down A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) on top of their other skill-position issues, so if Henry can go, he could see a considerable amount of targets against the Packers. He didn’t practice Wednesday or Thursday, however, so it seems unlikely. Eli Raridon is inline to be the top tight end option if Henry can’t play.

Source: WEEI

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: TreVeyon Henderson (illness) has been ruled out for Week 9 against the Packers.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

It seemed pretty obvious that Henderson wasn’t going to play Sunday after it was announced the second-year runner was dealing with “neurological symptoms” but it’s now official. There are much bigger things than football going on in his life. While he gets better, Corey Kiner should be the backup running back behind Rhamondre Stevenson going forward.

Source: WEEI

Rotoworld Author: Christopher Crawford
item.rw:author: Christopher Crawford

item.title: Joe Fagnano completed 10-of-18 passes for 60 yards and two interceptions in the Ravens’ 33-10, Week 9 loss to the Jaguars, adding 13 yards on three carries.
item.description:
Joe Fagnano BAL Quarterback

Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything he could to scheme around a starting undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first NFL start, calling numerous exotic looks to include direct snaps to Derrick Henry, a Henry pass attempt, quick outs to Zay Flowers, Flowers rush attempts, and flea flickers, but it wasn’t enough to overcome poor execution, consistently off-target throws, and a lack of downfield ability. The Ravens also committed numerous pre-snap penalties as they continue to lead the league in that area through nine weeks, which killed multiple drives. Fagnano managed only 25 pass yards in the first half, finishing with a ridiculous 60 yards, while both interceptions came in the second half with the team in desperation mode. Fagnano leaves his first, and likely last, NFL start with a sour taste in his mouth, as he likely retreats to backup duties following the signing of veteran Jacoby Brissett earlier in the week.

item.title: Brenton Strange caught both targets for 22 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Brenton Strange

Strange was overshadowed by the 52-yard reception from fellow tight end Nate Boerkircher on the team’s opening possession, but he made a really nice grab in triple coverage over the middle of the field to set up the team’s second score of the game. Strange remains unlikely to see consistent volume for as long as the Jaguars continue to so handily control games, something that appears likely to continue given the team holds the weakest strength of schedule for the remainder of the regular season. Fantasy managers likely have better options ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

item.title: Parker Washington caught 2-of-7 targets for 61 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Parker Washington

Both of Washington’s receptions came before the break, the second of which was a 50-yard touchdown on a double-move slant against Cover-0 with under one minute remaining before the half. Washington remains one of the most efficient receivers in the league but consistently positive game scripts have left the overall pass volume lacking, particularly in the second half this season. He remains an upside WR2 ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

item.title: Jakobi Meyers caught 4-of-6 targets for 65 yards in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Jakobi Meyers

All four of Meyers’ receptions came before the half in what remained a tighter game until just before the half, when alpha wide receiver Parker Washington took a simple slant for a 50-yard touchdown with under a minute remaining before the break. As has been the case on numerous occasions this season, Jacksonville coasted in the second half, limiting overall pass volume after the break. Meyers narrowly missed his first touchdown since Week 3 as he was tackled at the one on the team’s first possession. He remains a viable FLEX option ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the Titans.

item.title: Chris Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

Rodriguez split time with lead back Bhayshul Tuten in the first half before soaking up most of the backfield work in the third quarter. Both backs would then cede primary duties to special team ace Ameer Abdullah in the fourth quarter when the game was well in hand. Rodriguez has seen his fantasy value plummet of late with the emergence of Tuten as a borderline workhorse, a situation that was heavily influenced by Tuten’s lack of practice ahead of Thursday Night Football. The long week appears likely to provide the time needed for Tuten to return to full strength, leaving Rodriguez as a touchdown-dependent FLEX when the Jaguars face the Titans in Week 10.

item.title: Bhayshul Tuten rushed 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

Tuten started after failing to practice in any capacity this week, capping off the opening drive with a score from one yard out. He would split time with Chris Rodriguez for the rest of the first half before giving way to the combination of Rodriguez and special teams ace Ameer Abdullah for the bulk of the second half with the game in hand. Tuten should see his volume tick back up toward lead back territory when the Jaguars face off against the Titans in Week 10, where he will return to RB2 status.

item.title: Trevor Lawrence completed 16-of-26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ 33-10, Week 9 win over the Ravens.
item.description:
Trevor Lawrence

It was business as usual for Lawrence and the Jaguars, who won their eighth game by 20 or more points since the start of the 2025 season, the most in the league during that span. Lawrence looked sharp throughout, starting things off with a touchdown drive on their opening possession that was sparked by a 52-yard completion to tight end Nate Boerkircher. He would hit Parker Washington on a slant for a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the half to push the lead to 17-3, with a flurry of second half field goals enough to chase the reeling Ravens from the field. In standard Jacksonville fashion, positive game script capped Lawrence’s aerial volume, something fantasy managers have both gotten used to through the mid way point in the season and will likely see continue considering the Jaguars hold the league’s softest remaining strength of schedule. The win pushes the Jaguars to 6-2 and extends their lead in the AFC South ahead of a Week 10 meeting with the one-win Titans, where Lawrence will remain a back end QB1 due to lack of volume.

item.title: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reports that the Ravens are willing to make Lamar Jackson the highest-paid player in NFL history.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Well, that’s good, because it will assuredly take a record-setting deal to keep him in a Ravens uniform. Jackson has an $84.34 million salary cap hit next season, so the team has to do something with his contract. Jackson has a no-trade clause and a no-franchise tag clause — he possesses a ton of leverage. Per Palmer, the two sides will not negotiate a new deal in-season, so they will try to get something done between the end of the season and the beginning of free agency, which starts in March 2027.

Source: James Palmer

item.title: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Michael Wilson ARI Wide Receiver

Wilson will face the Seahawks this weekend, barring a setback. It’s a tough matchup, but Wilson’s target volume keeps him worth of remaining in starting lineups. Wilson showed decent chemistry with Gardner Minshew last week, which was nice to see, now that Jacoby Brissett is headed to the Ravens.

Source: Arizona Cardinals

item.title: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

Shaheed seems likely to miss another week, though he could technically still turn things around tomorrow. Seahawks LT Charles Cross (ankle) also remains sidelined on Thursday, and LG Quenton Nelson (knee) was downgraded to a non-participant. Hopefully, Nelson’s absence is precautionary.

Source: Andrew Destin

item.title: Drew Lock (elbow) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Lock has been dealing with an injury in his throwing arm since Week 7, but he told reporters that he is feeling good now. Lock played very well as Sam Darnold’s replacement earlier this year. As long as the elbow holds up, Lock should be expected to do so again. He is a viable QB2.

Source: Andrew Destin

item.title: Jordyn Tyson (hamstring) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Jordyn Tyson NO Wide Receiver

The Saints’ first-round rookie is now on the wrong side of questionable. It would have been nice to see him practice in full today. That said, New Orleans Football’s Nick Underhill commented positively on Tyson’s performance, saying Tyson “does not look limited.”

Source: Nick Underhill

item.title: Alvin Kamara (NIR-rest/back) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

The way the team listed Kamara indicates that the back injury will not keep him from playing, but he is clearly still hurt. Kamara has been entirely ineffective this season and can only be viewed as a touchdown-dependent FLEX. CJ Donaldson (concussion/shoulder) was unable to practice today.

Source: New Orleans Saints

item.title: Myles Garrett (knee) limited again on Thursday.
item.description:
Myles Garrett

Garrett has a chance to face the Commanders this week, but he still belongs in the questionable column at this time. Rams CB1 Trent McDuffie (back) and S Kam Curl (foot) both missed practice for the second time this week.

Source: Ben Standig

item.title: Matthew Stafford (right elbow) practiced in full on Thursday.
item.description:
Matthew Stafford

Stafford has downplayed inquiries regarding his throwing-arm injury, saying he’s been icing his elbow post-game and post-practice for a while now — and he called out the beat reporters for missing it. Lingering elbow soreness isn’t exactly reassuring, but at least he is practicing fully. Stafford should be good to go for the Rams’ Week 9 game against the Commanders, but this is obviously worth monitoring.

Source: Nate Atkins

item.title: David Njoku (fibula) was limited on Thursday.
item.description:
David Njoku LAC Tight End

Njoku’s return is probably a good thing for the offense as a whole, but the Chargers’ tight end rotation makes for a fantasy-unfriendly situation. Njoku does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats. Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) remains sidelined.

Source: Los Angeles Chargers

item.title: Travon Walker (ribs) is active for Week 9 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Travon Walker

The Jaguars’ No. 2 edge rusher will play through his ribs injury tonight. He apparently got hurt during Tuesday’s practice, but is good to go two days later. The Jaguars declared WR CJ Williams, CB Alijah Huzzie, S Cam’Ron Silmon-Craig and DE Wesley Williams inactive for Week 9 against the Ravens.

Source: Jacksonville Jaguars

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer reports that the Eagles have received “a ton of interest” on the trade market for Moro Ojomo.
item.description:
Moro Ojomo PHI Defensive Tackle

Ojomo is in a contract year, and per Breer, the Eagles have told interested parties that they would like to keep him beyond this year. With both Jalen Carter and Jordan Davis signed for multiple seasons, investing heavily in another defensive tackle might be cost-prohibitive. Perhaps the Eagles are simply trying to drive up Ojomo’s trade value. Stay tuned.

Source: Albert Breer

item.title: Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer thinks the Titans might be willing to trade away Tony Pollard in exchange for a fourth-round pick.
item.description:
Tony Pollard TEN Running Back

Breer believes a fourth-round pick “seems like a lot” to give up for an aging running back who is set to enter free agency at the end of the year. So, Pollard might end up staying in Tennessee. Breer adds that the Titans could also consider trading away Calvin Ridley for a worse Day 3 pick, but he isn’t sure if the team is eager to get rid of pass catchers while they are attempting to develop their young quarterback.

Source: Albert Breer

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) is “good to go” after completing his pre-game workout for Week 9 against the Ravens.
item.description:
Bhayshul Tuten

The Jaguars have routinely killed the clock with their efficient ground game this season, oftentimes pulling Trevor Lawrence early. With the Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano (ankle) tonight, the Jaguars should again enjoy a run-heavy game script, expectedly playing with a lead. Tuten is an RB1, having avoided suffering a setback this week.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Derrick Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens’ Week 9 loss to the Jaguars.
item.description:
Derrick Henry BAL Running Back

Offensive coordinator Declan Doyle did everything in his power to overcome an undrafted free agent rookie quarterback in his first professional start, going so far as numerous direct snaps to Henry and a Henry pass attempt, but it ultimately proved futile. Things appeared to be trending in the right direction as the Ravens played the Jaguars to a tightly contested game through the first 29 minutes before Parker Washington broke the game open with a 50-yard touchdown in the final minute before the break. Things got nasty for Henry after the half as he managed only two additional yards after bruising his way to 55 first half yards. Henry will return to RB1 status in fantasy circles in Week 10 when the Ravens take on the Chargers.

item.title: Chris Rodriguez rushed 10 times for 19 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars’ Week 9 win over the Ravens, adding 13 yards on two receptions.
item.description:
Chris Rodriguez

Rodriguez split time with lead back Bayshul Tuten in the first half before soaking up most of the backfield work in the third quarter. Both backs would then cede primary duties to special team ace Ameer Abdullah in the fourth quarter when the game was well in hand. Rodriguez has seen his fantasy value plummet of late with the emergence of Tuten as a borderline workhorse, a situation that was heavily influenced by Tuten’s lack of practice ahead of Thursday Night Football. The long week appears likely to provide the time needed for Tuten to return to full strength, leaving Rodriguez as a touchdown-dependent FLEX when the Jaguars face the Titans in Week 10.

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports Carson Wentz is “trending toward” starting in Week 9 against the Bills.
item.description:
Carson Wentz MIN Quarterback

Kyler Murray suffered a hamstring injury in Week 8, but even Schefter alluded to the idea that this would be a soft benching for Murray. Schefter added that it “looks like there’s a question at the quarterback position” for Minnesota. Healthy or not, it sounds like Wentz is going to be under center versus Buffalo. Wentz made one start earlier in the season while Murray was sidelined with a concussion. He only threw for 133 yards on 19 attempts, but Wentz found the end zone three times. Murray hasn’t thrown three passing touchdowns in a game since the end of the 2024 season. Wentz’s gunslinging style will likely be a win for fantasy managers hoping to get more out of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison, especially in a potential shootout with the Bills.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: NFL insider Jordan Schultz reports the Colts plan to wait until after Week 9 against the Cowboys “before revisiting the offers on the table and making the trades that make sense on Monday and Tuesday.”
item.description:
Jonathan Taylor IND Running Back

Long story short, the Colts are trying to wring every last ounce of draft capital out of their roster and think teams will up their offers after Sunday’s games. Schultz named Jonathan Taylor, Josh Downs, and Grover Stewart as players who could be on the move. Daniel Jones’s name has also come up, though it’s hard to imagine another team paying even a late-round pick for his services given how dreadful he has been this year. All signs point to Taylor being moved early next week, but it’s clear the Colts are going to play hardball in trade talks. We still suspect he’s playing for a new team by Week 10.

Source: Jordan Schultz

item.title: Grady Jarrett (groin) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
item.description:
Grady Jarrett CHI Defensive Lineman

Jarrett played in Week 8 against the Seahawks after missing Week 7 with a knee injury and now is an estimated DNP with a groin injury to open Week 9. He still has a chance to play, but will need at least a limited practice to appear against the Buccaneers.

item.title: Kyle Monangai (thumb/toe) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
item.description:
Kyle Monangai CHI Running Back

Monangai was an estimated DNP on Wednesday, still not practicing in any capacity since Week 4. He has missed four consecutive games and is trending to miss a fifth one in Week 9 against the Buccaneers. In any injury taking this long for a return, a full practice is the best indicator of a return but the Bears may just wait until after their Week 10 bye to bring Monangai back. D’Andre Swift is in line for a workhorse game once again.

item.title: Kenneth Gainwell (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Gainwell played through the hip injury last week to the tune of 25 carries. He starts out the week limited, but fantasy managers should expect to see the 27-year-old to play in Week 9 against the Bears.

item.title: Leonard Williams (stinger) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
item.description:
Leonard Williams SEA Defensive Tackle

Williams suffered a stinger in Week 8 and was an estimated DNP for the Seahawks’ walkthrough practice on Wednesday. The veteran will need to practice in some capacity to have a chance to play in Week 9 against the Cardinals. If not, the Seahawks’ interior defensive line will be reinforced by Mike Morris, who notched his first career sack against the Bears in Week 8.

item.title: Rashid Shaheed (knee) did not practice in Wednesday’s walkthrough.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

Also not practicing is OT Charles Cross (ankle). Both missed Week 8 against the Bears and are still out with their respective injuries to open the week. They will need to practice in some fashion to have a chance at returning for the Seahawks offense in Week 9.

item.title: Drew Lock (elbow) was limited in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
item.description:
Drew Lock SEA Quarterback

Despite being listed as limited with a right elbow injury, Lock is expected to start in place of Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) in Week 9 against the Cardinals. Lock has been dealing with the elbow injury for a couple weeks and was the emergency third quarterback in Week 8 as a result. Fantasy managers can still expect Lock to start, but if the injury is not healed, Jalen Milroe is the next quarterback up for the Seahawks.

item.title: Reggie Virgil (back) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Reggie Virgil ARI Wide Receiver

Virgil practiced fully after colliding with the goalpost in the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys. It’s a good sign that his back is not a major issue heading into the week. He’s in line to play in Week 9 against the Seahawks.

item.title: Bam Knight (concussion) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Zonovan Knight ARI Running Back

Knight entered concussion protocol after a hit to the head in Week 8 against the Cowboys. Starting out as a DNP this week means he still has a few steps to go to clear protocol by Sunday. Unless he can progress through protocol quickly, Knight is on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Seahawks.

item.title: ESPN’s Rob Demovsky reports Josh Jacobs is “operating under the assumption” he won’t miss more games despite additional allegations of abuse against him.
item.description:
Josh Jacobs GB Running Back

Jacobs is facing additional allegations of verbal and physical abuse that could jeopardize his playing status moving forward. He told Demovsky that he is “operating under the assumption that he won’t have to sit out any more games than the six he already missed while on the NFL commissioner exempt list.” Jacobs has defended himself against the allegations after his attorneys also dismissed the claims. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said earlier this week he expects Jacobs to remain on the roster as the league reviews this round of allegations. Jacobs has missed six games on the Commissioner’s Exempt List and will continue to play while the NFL looks into the new claims.

Source: Rob Demovsky

item.title: Arthur Maulet retired after nine seasons in the NFL.
item.description:
Arthur Maulet

NFL Network’s Cameron Wolfe reports that Maulet is retiring. The 33-year-old slot cornerback began his career with the Saints and Colts and ended it with the Lions, but made the bulk of his impact from 2019-2024 with the Jets, Steelers, and Ravens. Maulet made major noise as a hard-hitting cornerback in the AFC North, going from the Steelers to the Ravens in 2023 and starting a playoff game for Mike Macdonald’s historic Ravens defense. He retires with five career interceptions and five sacks.

Source: Cameron Wolfe

item.title: Treylon Burks (foot) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Treylon Burks WAS Wide Receiver

Burks was limited-DNP-limited due to the foot injury last week, but played through it for five targets in the Commanders’ Week 8 win over the Eagles. He starts out this week as a DNP as the Commanders manage his injury. Given he already played a game with the injury, Burks is still likely to play in Week 9, though he will need to get a practice in later this week to feel better about his chances of playing against the Rams.

item.title: David Njoku (fibula) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
David Njoku LAC Tight End

Njoku had his practice window opened this week, giving the Chargers 21 days to activate him off injured reserve. He has been out since Week 3 and is now nearing a return, getting in limited work with a fibula injury on Wednesday. WR Brenen Thompson (quad/hamstring) was a DNP on Wednesday. Neither Njoku nor Thompson need to be on fantasy rosters just yet.

item.title: Seahawks signed QB Adrian Martinez to the practice squad.
item.description:
Adrian Martinez SEA Quarterback

Martinez has bounced around the 49ers and Jets in the NFL, while winning MVP in the UFL in 2024. He worked out for the Ravens earlier this week but now joins the Seahawks as depth with Sam Darnold (quad) banged up and set to miss Week 9 against the Cardinals.

Source: Brady Henderson

item.title: Christian Kirk (knee) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

Kirk comes out of the 49ers’ bye as a limited practice participant due to a knee issue. He was not targeted in Week 7 after returning off a calf injury and should remain off fantasy rosters even if he plays in Week 9 against the Raiders.

item.title: Reed Blankenship (consussion/hand) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Reed Blankenship HOU Safety

Blankenship has been dealing with a concussion since Week 6 and still has it listed as an injury designation nearly three weeks later. He is also listed with a hand injury. Blankenship will need to progress through concussion protocol to have a chance at playing in Week 9; he is on the wrong side of questionable for now.

item.title: Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles said RB Kenneth Gainwell’s usage is getting closer to the “1A, 1B” usage the team envisioned when signing him.
item.description:
Kenny Gainwell TB Running Back

Gainwell saw 25 carries in a run-heavy game against the Falcons in Week 8. Bowles said, “I think we finally got to where we’re utilizing Kenny more and more, and that’s kind of the 1A, 1B we were talking about when we first signed him.” Gainwell saw 50-percent of the snaps for the first time all season last week and now has back-to-back weeks of at least 14 carries. He is still seeing low utilization in the passing game and game script has certainly played a role in his recent role, but it is notable that Bowles mentions the Bucs envisioned a 1A/1B backfield pairing between Bucky Irving and Gainwell. Despite Bowles’ comments, fantasy managers should anticipate Irving operating with the majority of backfield touches, like he did from Weeks 1-6. We will still have to see Gainwell’s usage in a more neutral game script to feel confident about him as a fantasy option moving forward.

Source: MicNuggets

item.title: Jihaad Campbell (hamstring/quad) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Jihaad Campbell PHI Linebacker

Campbell missed the Eagles’ Week 8 game against the Commanders after not practicing all of last week due to hamstring and quad injuries. He starts out this week DNP, along with DBs Michael Carter (abdomen) and Jonathan Jones (hamstring) on the defensive side of the ball. All three will need some kind of practice later in the week to have a chance at reinforcing the Eagles defense in Week 9 against the Giants.

item.title: Jake Elliot (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jake Elliott PHI Kicker

Elliot was listed as a limited participant for the Eagles’ Wednesday practice. The 31-year-old has made 6-of-7 field goals this season and all 17 extra points. He is still trending to play in Week 9, but if the Eagles add another kicker sometime this week, that would indicate Elliot’s ankle injury is a real issue.

item.title: Trent McDuffie (back) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

McDuffie played through a groin injury in Week 8 and seemingly picked up a new back injury during the game. Rams head coach Sean McVay said McDuffie will be a DNP Wednesday, indicating the 26-year-old’s back issue is more than a minor flare-up. It’s possible he is getting the day off to rest the groin and back injuries, but Rams fans should keep an eye on his practice status the rest of the week. It’s safe to say McDuffie is truly questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.

item.title: Colby Parkinson (ribs) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Colby Parkinson

Rams head coach Sean McVay announced Parkinson would be a DNP on Wednesday. The 27-year-old has been dealing with a rib injury since Week 7, missing the Rams’ Week 8 game against the Chargers. Starting out DNP puts him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 9 against the Commanders.

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (chest) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle played through a questionable tag with this injury last week, catching 3-of-6 targets for 39 yards and one touchdown against the Chiefs. He apparently made it through the contest without re-injuring himself and can be started as a WR3 this week against the Panthers.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: Pat Bryant (ankle) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Pat Bryant DEN Wide Receiver

Bryant’s 21-day practice window has been opened, and it begins with a full session, putting him on track to play in Week 9 against the Panthers. The Broncos’ passing game has severely underperformed expectations. Bryant does not necessarily need to be added in 12-team formats, though he could ultimately compete for No. 2 wide receiver duties.

Source: Denver Broncos

item.title: The Athletic’s Nate Atkins believes the Rams must find a way to trade for a wide receiver before the November 10th deadline.
item.description:
Josh Downs IND Wide Receiver

The Rams’ resources are thin. They already traded away their 2027 first- and second-round picks, their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. They also have just $8,000 in 2026 salary cap space, so restructuring the potential new add’s deal would be required. Atkins believes the Rams should consider Josh Downs as the top option due to his ability to beat man coverage and contribute as a returner. Other options, according to Atkins, include Calvin Ridley, Keenan Allen and Jauan Jennings, “for the likely cost of a Day 3 pick.”

Source: The Athletic

item.title: Raiders released WR Cody White.
item.description:
Cody White

Tight end Carter Runyon was activated from injured reserve in a corresponding move. White has eight catches for 112 yards and three scores this year. He also contributes on special teams. The Raiders could ultimately sign him to their practice squad and promote him to the game-day roster this week.

Source: Sam Warren

item.title: Jaylen Wright (quad) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

Dolphins RB3 Kaytron Allen (quad) was limited. At some point, Allen might get a chance to overtake Wright for the No. 2 role, though Wright remains a capable special teams contributor.

Source: Marcel Louis-Jacques

item.title: Kadyn Proctor (concussion) is practicing in full for Week 9 against the Lions.
item.description:
Kadyn Proctor MIA Offensive Lineman

The Dolphins’ starting left guard should make his return this week after sitting out in Week 8 against the Patriots. Proctor’s presence will help stabilize the pocket for Malik Willis.

Source: Marcel Louis-Jacques

item.title: Christian Watson (rib) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

Watson famously left for the hospital in the middle of Week 8’s win over the Panthers, only to return after halftime like a WWE performer. The fact that they’re letting him practice in any capacity today means he should be able to play through the issue in Week 9. We’d expect him to wear a flak jacket for at least a few weeks. Barring a setback in practice, Watson will be a high-variance WR1 for his matchup with the Patriots.
